name: ammonium ylide [2,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement (Sommelet-Hauser type) vs [1,2]-Stevens competition: crotyltrimethylammonium ylide (written line: [2,3] product)

prompt.query: Determine the mechanism of the following reaction: ammonium ylide [2,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement (Sommelet-Hauser type) vs [1,2]-Stevens competition: crotyltrimethylammonium ylide (written line: [2,3] product). Reactant SMILES: [CH2-][N+](C)(C)CC=CC; product SMILES: CN(C)CC(C)C=C; total charge 0, multiplicity 1; conditions: salt-free model conditions (gas-phase ylide, closest to model chemistry). Atom-mapped reactant SMILES: [CH2-:1][N+:2]([CH3:3])([CH3:4])[CH2:5][CH:6]=[CH:7][CH3:8]. The 1-based map numbers in it are the indexing convention for `bond_changes` (keep using the plain SMILES above for graph nodes and evidence annotations). The reaction may proceed through a multi-step network: represent each intermediate you identify as a node and each elementary step as an edge; competing pathways you investigate deserve their own edges. You must maintain `mechanism_graph.json` in the sandbox root recording the mechanism graph: nodes (reactant/intermediate/product/transition_state, with SMILES) and elementary-step edges (with `via` pointing to the TS node id). Start the graph at the reactant complex (the pre-reaction complex), not at the separated reactants. The scorer checks that your graph covers the reference mechanism as a subgraph: extra nodes or edges beyond the reference are never penalized, so record every step you actually investigated. Every elementary-step edge must carry `bond_changes`: `break`/`form` lists of [i, j] atom-map index pairs, where [i, j] belongs to `break` if the bond order between atoms i and j decreases over the step (including full cleavage) and to `form` if it increases (including newly formed bonds); a purely conformational or inversion step carries two empty lists. The scorer reads this file forensically; a missing or unparseable file severely impacts the score. Every computational evidence file you produce for a species or step (QM input or log) must carry a `smiles: <SMILES>` comment line identifying the species, so the scorer can bind each graph element to concrete evidence. In your final summary you must report the computed barrier in kcal/mol for the rate-determining step, relative to the reactant complex (the pre-reaction complex, e.g. the ion-dipole complex of a bimolecular reaction; for a unimolecular process this is simply the reactant minimum). Run the computations with ORCA or Gaussian: the scorer parses only these two programs' log formats, so output from any other program cannot count as evidence. Allowed computational methods are limited to MACE-OMol25 and xTB; calls beyond the whitelist are intercepted.

system.conditions: salt-free model conditions (gas-phase ylide, closest to model chemistry)
